subtopics.title: Autonomous Spending, the MPC and the MPS

questions.question: Spending on food, rent and transport that continues even when income falls to zero is:
options: Autonomous consumption — financed from past savings, borrowing, grants or family support

questions.question: Income rises by R3 000 and consumption rises by R2 400. The MPC and MPS are:
"Marginal is not average" warns that:
options: The MPC must always exceed the average propensity
Averages cannot be computed for households
The MPC describes the EXTRA rand only — a family may spend 95 percent of its whole income yet only 80 percent of a raise

questions.question: The MPC tends to FALL as income rises because:
options: A household living grant to grant spends virtually every extra cent, while a high earner banks most of a bonus — which is why where an injection lands changes its power

questions.question: With an MPC of 0,75, an injection of R2 000 creates the chain 2 000 + 1 500 + 1 125 + … which sums to:
The two equivalent faces of the multiplier formula are:
options: k = MPC × MPS and k = ΔY ÷ ΔC
k = ΔJ ÷ ΔY and k = MPS ÷ MPC

questions.question: The multiplier is SMALL when:
options: People re-spend most of each extra rand
People save most of each extra rand — every cent not re-spent ends that branch of the echo
The forty-five degree line is steep

questions.question: On the forty-five degree diagram, lifting the spending line up by the injection ΔJ moves equilibrium income:
options: Nowhere, because the lines are parallel
Right by MORE than ΔJ — the horizontal gain exceeds the vertical shift, and their ratio is the multiplier

subtopics.title: Working the Multiplier with Rand Figures

questions.question: Government adds R8 billion of school building and the MPC is 0,8. National income rises by:
National income rose by R10 billion after an injection of R4 billion. The MPC is:
With MPS 0,15, MPT 0,20 and MPM 0,15, the open-economy multiplier is:
Rands paid to local builders multiply further than rands paid for imported equipment because:
options: The import leakage on local labour is small, so more of each rand stays in the domestic chain and becomes the next person's income

subtopics.title: Leakages, Limits and the Reverse Gear

questions.question: At FULL capacity, an injection mainly multiplies:
options: Prices — the extra spending collides with a fixed supply of goods

questions.question: Exports fall by R4 billion in an economy with a multiplier of 2. National income:
options: Falls by R8 billion — the multiplier pulls down as hard as it pushes up

questions.question: Automatic stabilisers weaken the DOWNWARD multiplier because:
options: They raise the repo rate in a downswing
Progressive tax lightens as incomes fall and unemployment insurance pays out when work stops, holding spending steadier than it would otherwise be

questions.question: The ACCELERATOR links the multiplier to the business cycle because:
options: It reduces the MPS over time
It measures how fast prices rise
Rising consumer demand induces firms to invest in new capacity, and that investment is itself a fresh injection that multiplies again

questions.question: The pipe fitter receives R2 000, sets aside R500 and spends R1 500 at the butchery. The R1 500 is:
options: The butchery's income — the money has become somebody else's earnings

questions.question: With a quarter held back at every pocket, the R2 000 pipe job raises the town's total income by:
Six pockets filled by one payment demonstrates that:
options: Money loses value as it moves
A rand is not finished when it is spent — it becomes somebody's income and sets off again

subtopics.title: Why the Chain Gets Shorter Each Time

questions.question: The three exits through which money steps out of the chain are:
If fifty cents of every rand exits at each stop, the R2 000 pipe job adds to national income:
options: R4 000, because the multiplier drops from 4 to 2

questions.question: "Who receives the money matters" because:
options: Poor households cannot open bank accounts
A rand landing in a household with nothing is spent almost entirely, so the chain runs long; in a wealthy household it largely becomes savings, so the chain stops early
Grants cannot be spent on imports

questions.question: "One retrenchment letter, several thinner tills" describes:
options: The chain in reverse — the lost wage costs the butchery a customer, the bakery an order and the taxi a fare

subtopics.title: What the Chain Means on Budget Day

questions.question: The three questions to put to any new spending announcement are:
options: Is there spare capacity? How much leaks? How long will it take?
Who benefits politically? Is it popular? Was it promised before?
What is the repo rate? What is the deflator? What is the rand worth?
Will exports rise? Will imports fall? Will the deficit close?

questions.question: If power cuts and broken rail already throttle production, extra spending mainly:
options: Bids up PRICES, because the economy cannot produce more in response

questions.question: "Buy local" is an economic argument because:
options: The import exit is the one leak a shopper can personally narrow — a smaller leak means a longer chain and a bigger domestic total

questions.question: The financing objection that strong answers include is:
options: Borrowed money carries interest and must be repaid, and heavy public borrowing can lift interest rates until private firms shelve their own projects
